title: WASM-based runbook-as-service: sandboxed operator actions with idempotency and audit
creator: Sana Gupta
description: Build a runbook-as-service that runs small, idempotent operator actions inside a WebAssembly sandbox. The goal is to provide safe, auditable operator utilities that can be invoked from the Console, Slack, or automated remediation pipelines. This service will expose a typed API for registering runbook templates, validating inputs, performing dry-runs, and executing with strict time/resource limits and RBAC-scoped ephemeral tokens.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prototype WASM action runner that executes a simple 'rotate-credentials' action with CPU and memory limits. 2) Runbook registration API supporting typed schema and 'dry_run' flag. 3) Audit records emitted to the existing ops-audit log with request provenance and KV diff. 4) Console UI button to trigger runbook with parameter validation and confirmation workflow. 5) Canary automation that replays runbook in a non-destructive mode before production rollout.
updates: 2025-01-10 - Ticket created by Sana: initial proposal for WASM-based sandbox after onboarding chat with SRE. Identified need for idempotent primitives and audit provenance.
2025-01-16 - Architecture sync: decided to embed wasmtime for sandboxing; runtime will run in a per-tenant ephemeral worker pool. Liam to spike resource limiter and policy enforcement.

2025-01-22 - Spike results: WASM runner can enforce CPU/memory/timeouts and prevent syscalls; trade-off: larger binary size and cold-start overhead. Proposed mitigations: warm pool + lightweight caching of modules.
2025-01-28 - Security review request created (confluence link above). Discussed token model: short-lived per-invocation scoped token with least-privilege and KMS-backed signing.
2025-02-05 - Implemented runbook registration API prototype and JSONSchema parameter validation. Added dry_run flag that exercises validation and returns a simulated diff without mutating state.

2025-02-12 - Integrated audit events with ops-audit pipeline. Events include: invoker, runbook_id, inputs (redacted fields marked), start/finish timestamps, and produced diffs. Dashboards updated for visibility.
2025-02-18 - Console UX prototype: added 'Run' button for experimental runbooks. Includes an interstitial confirm dialog and optional escalation flow for higher-risk actions.
2025-02-25 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/operator-automation/pull/238 titled 'wasm-runner: add worker pool and audit hooks' — requesting review from Maya and Priya.
2025-02-28 - Current blockers: need final sign-off on token minting flow from Security; brief perf regression on cold-starts observed in load test (p95 latency spike).
